title: HeaderDateTime derives Copy: future non-Copy fields force a breaking change
description:
header_typed.rs:67 — `#[derive(..., Copy, ...)]` on HeaderDateTime.

Current fields are all small primitives so Copy is cheap. But the derive locks in a contract that every future field must also be Copy. Likely future additions that break this:

- Sub-second precision via a `Duration`-like or `String` for fractional seconds (not Copy if String).
- An IANA timezone name like `tz_name: Option<String>` (not Copy).
- A `calendar: CalendarSystem` enum that grows non-Copy variants.

Removing the Copy derive once shipped is a breaking change — callers depending on `*dt` or implicit copy semantics break at compile time. RustCrypto and other Rust-API guideline tradition is to derive Copy only when the type is genuinely a "wide register": short, fixed-width, ABI-stable primitive bag. A wire-format date with future expansion is borderline.

Caller-facing consequence: maintainer can never add a non-Copy field without breaking every caller that relies on Copy semantics. The choice should be deliberate.

Fix: either (a) drop Copy now while still pre-1.0 and document `.clone()` as the canonical copy path, or (b) keep Copy and explicitly commit in module docs that the struct will remain Copy forever — accepting that subsecond precision and similar additions are off the table.
close_reason: Type-definition cleanup batch on the typed header surface: (.4) added #[non_exhaustive] to EmailAddress and AddressGroup (HeaderDateTime was already done); (.5) dropped Copy from HeaderDateTime; (.26) dropped Copy from HeaderForm; (.18/.19/.20) added Display impls — RFC 5322 §3.4 mailbox/group form for EmailAddress/AddressGroup, RFC 3339 form for HeaderDateTime; (.34/.35) added Hash on EmailAddress/AddressGroup/HeaderDateTime/HeaderValueTyped; (.36) added Default on EmailAddress/AddressGroup; (.33) symmetric by-value internal signature on to_mail_parser/from_mail_parser. New public constructors EmailAddress::new and AddressGroup::new for callers blocked by #[non_exhaustive]. New tests cover Display, Hash, and TzSign.
